title: Protocol for multispectral imaging on cryosections to map myeloid cell heterogeneity in its spatial context
protocol: Collect fresh, unfixed tissue samples.
Place the tissue, with the cutting plane down, in a labelled cryomold and add OCT compound until the tissue is completely covered.
Transfer the cryomold into a dry ice-cooled container of isopentane and let it float until the OCT has solidified.
Store the cryomold on dry ice until all samples are collected and store them at −80°C in sealed bags or wrapped in aluminum foil to minimize drying out.
Cut 7 μm thick cryosections using a Cryostat (e.g., CM 3050, Leica) and collect them on sequential microscopy slides.
Dry the slides in a desiccator for several hours at room temperature before storing them at −80°C.
Air-dry tissue sections completely before freezing to prevent crystallization.
Use conductive indium tin oxide (ITO) slides to mount tissue sections for mass spectrometry imaging.
Cut tissue sections from non-embedded snap frozen tissue instead of using OCT medium.
Store cut tissue sections on ITO slides at −20°C without dehydrating them.
Follow manufacturer's recommendations for specific slides and/or collection areas for spatial transcriptomics.
Fix cryosections.
Block cryosections.
Optionally bleach cryosections.
Thaw cryosections.
Air-dry cryosections.
Fix cryosections with dry acetone for 5 minutes.
Immerse slides in blocking buffer.
Optional: Expose slides to high-power near-UV light overnight in a cold room (4°C).
For tissues with high autofluorescence, perform an autofluorescence bleaching step prior to staining.
Dilute antibodies individually in cold blocking buffer containing 7-AAD nuclear dye just prior to staining.
Apply antibody solution on tissue sections and incubate for 4 h in the dark at 4°C.
Wash three times with PBS.
Mount coverslip with 50 μL water-based antifade mounting medium (e.g., Prolong Gold).
Leave the mounted slides to dry for 60 min at room temperature (around 20°C) in the dark before imaging or storing at 4°C.
Define the mean emission spectrum over several pixels with sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratio.
Check if the detected spectrum corresponds with the theoretical spectrum (as provided by the manufacturer).
Assess the risk of bleed-through in other spectra and image cubes.
Save the spectrum in the spectral library as a reference for this dye.
Unmix the image cube into background and dye-specific signal components to assess the specificity of the newly defined spectrum.
Fix and bleach cryosections.
Repeat procedure as in Step 2.
Dilute antibodies included in the complete antibody panel using the appropriate titration in cold blocking buffer.
Apply the antibody mix on PAP pen-lined tissue sections.
Incubate the slides for 4 hours in the dark at 4°C.
Wash the slides 3 times by fully immersing them in PBS.
If required, incubate another 60 minutes with secondary antibodies specific for not more than one of the primary antibodies.
Wash again 3 times with PBS.
Mount coverslip with 50 μL water-based antifade mountant (e.g., Prolong Gold).
Leave slides to dry for 60 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Store the slides at 4°C in the dark until the next day for imaging.
Acquire image cubes for every region of interest.
Unmix the image cubes based on their corresponding spectral libraries to obtain single channel grayscale images.
Save each grayscale image as a .jpg file.
Save all images from the same field of view in a shared folder with consistent names for automated analysis.
Do not move the tissue section between acquisitions with different excitation filters to maintain alignment of grayscale images.
Acquire multiple, non-overlapping images from one tissue section to better define cell subsets and reduce selection bias.
Use parallel cell type-specific markers or several phenotypic markers to distinguish subsets of a single cell type.
Include reporters of the cell’s status if desired to visualize cells within their cellular context.
Employ negative control and fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) stainings in case of high similarity between emission spectra for correct unmixing validation.
Submerge fluorescently imaged slides in PBS and leave them at 37°C until the cover slip spontaneously detaches (about 20–30 min).
Proceed with standard H&E staining.
Mount the slide with non-aqueous mounting medium (e.g., Prolong Gold) for long-term storage.
Acquire images of the same regions of interest that were fluorescently imaged, but at a lower magnification.
Download the 'AutoRegi_Nuance_HE.mlapp' app from GitHub.
Install it in MATLAB.
Add the 'Image processing Toolbox’ to your MATLAB.
Run the script, a pop-up window will appear.
Click “load” to open a fluorescent image of the nuclear staining (7-AAD) and the corresponding H&E image file (H&E) from the same tissue section.
Stay in the ‘manually’ panel to align the image manually by selecting landmarks on both fluorescent image and H&E image.
Select the ‘selectpoint’, and click ‘run’.
Click to place a crosshair on a recognizable landmark in one image and select the corresponding point in the other image.
Open an aligned H&E image and set the image type to Brightfield (H&E).
Select the whole image as region of interest or exclude irrelevant areas or artifacts.
Select Analyze > Cell detection > Cell detection.
Toggle off the ‘include cell nucleus’ option in the settings window.
Alter the settings until all cells are correctly segmented.
Copy the cell segmentation to ImageJ (Extensions > Image J > Send region to ImageJ).
In ImageJ, save the cell segments as a mask (Image > Overlay > to ROI manager; select all ROIs and save them as RoiSet.zip in the corresponding folder).
Overlay the saved masks on each of the fluorescent images.
Measure the mean dye intensity over each numbered segment using standard image analysis programs such as Cell profiler, ImageJ, QuPath or others.
